record.body:
## Architecture

1. Extend the manifest schema with `support_files` (paths relative to repo root) and include a stable digest of the `runner` argv in the frozen set authorize() covers.
2. Hash support file bytes at a revision the same way oracle files are hashed; surface hash-mismatch (or a dedicated reason) when support or runner digest changes without a covering amendment.
3. Ship a lint entry point (CLI subcommand or library function invoked by tests) that walks witness tests for missing assertions and compares skip/`not_run` sets between two revisions.
4. Tests cover support-only drift, runner-only drift, no-assert, and new-skip fixtures without weakening existing oracle amendment cases.

## Interfaces

- Manifest fields: `support_files: list[str]` (and/or per-claim support), runner digest derived from `runner`.
- Amendment canonical payload gains support hashes and runner digest.
- Lint: reports structured findings for no-assert and new-skip (exact CLI shape at plan-phase).

## Decisions

- `support-files-schema`: explicit support_files + runner digest under amendment rule.
- `freeze-lint`: separate lint for no-assert and new skips.
- `campaign-5-11`: this phase is the first of the autopilot batch; phase-end reviewer runs here.

## Invariants

- Unsigned support or runner drift cannot yield verdict pass.
- Store tokens stay out of `affidavit/`.

## Assumptions

- One support list granularity (manifest-global or per-claim) is enough; plan-phase picks the smaller change that meets R1.
- Lint may be `aff lint` or a pytest-invoked helper in this phase.

## Tradeoffs

- Explicit paths need authoring; a whole-tree hash would amend more often.
- Lint separate from verdict means a green verdict can still have lint findings unless plan-phase wires lint into verification.

## Risks

- Agents omit support paths and keep editing undeclared conftest. Mitigation: default recommendations in claim-authoring; tests that show the failure mode when declared.
- Runner digest churn from cosmetic argv reorder. Mitigation: canonicalize argv before digest.
